The latest expansion establishes two distinct Arbor identities and warns against combining their mechanisms, code, or effects.
AMD no-DFS ablation jointly removes structure and a revert path and ends in a crash; the critic ablation concerns measurement validity.

raw_finding.why_it_matters: A later source-faithful control or external anchor can select the wrong system or import the wrong ablation interpretation. The two Arbor papers study different interventions and do not supply interchangeable evidence. HTR additionally treats the tree and insight feedback as separate ablations; AMD no-DFS is the recovery-confounded result discussed in the latest update.
raw_finding.smallest_correction: In the next task-bound comparison record, resolve each inherited Arbor reference to exact arXiv ID/version, full title, source hash/locator, and intended mechanism. Link the existing source record if it already resolves the identity; do not rewrite frozen P0 or require a new general review.

If it already uniquely binds the intended HTR or AMD paper, add that explicit reference and close this item. Otherwise resolve the identifier before selecting the comparator. No experiment is needed.
raw_finding.uncertainty: The complete historical source graph and transitive predecessor source records were not supplied/read. They may already identify the intended Arbor, reducing this to an omitted direct link. No wrong implementation has been observed.

evidence.detail: End-to-end graph cost and equal hard ceilings are the intended comparison.
All future resource-envelope values remain null.
Operational arm table explicitly is not executable; prompt/tool/config, capsule byte ceilings and activation receipts remain null.
Common measurement boundaries and C/G research obligations must have distinct, equally enforced loci.
Latest synthesis retains matched rights, obligations, scheduler and recovery; no frozen arm implementation is supplied.
Current C0 protocol explicitly has between-message/sampled token enforcement, not a hard in-flight cap.

raw_finding.why_it_matters: G−C can identify the assigned graph-control package, but only once that package and its common substrate are defined. Differences in usable evidence delivery, critic/recovery opportunities, gate strength or uncharged graph work could otherwise become unintended treatment components. Equal consumption is not required; unequal certified limits or unreported overflow cannot support the stated fixed-resource interpretation.
raw_finding.minimum_correction: In the next P1 task contract, bind B/C/G prompt/tool/controller/capsule bytes, exact compulsory obligation predicates and gate locations, equivalent non-graph computation rights, common scheduler/opportunity ceilings, and all-descendant extraction/recovery/final-assessment costs. Declare actual budget enforcement and overshoot/unknown-cost rules. Preserve the current P0 monitored-cap scope instead of retroactively calling it hard enforcement.
raw_finding.inexpensive_falsification_check: Before model work, have a reviewer walk the same permitted source revision, stale-scope case and near-budget request through the three declared arm tables. Only declared treatment differences should change admissibility or delivered information. Account for a graph build and a recovery attempt in the same ledger; any free work, undeclared tool right, unequal common rejection or missing overflow rule refutes the matched implementation claim.
raw_finding.uncertainty: No B/C/G implementation or scientific trace was run or audited. This is an acknowledged unfilled specification, not evidence that a completed comparison is confounded.

raw_finding.phase: Metric and outcome table before P1; final confirmation analysis before P2

evidence.detail: Metric, aggregation, invalid handling and selection rule are null while single frozen final artifact is specified.
All-assigned census and non-fabrication are required, but exact metric-specific missingness rule is explicitly unset.
Agent selection, no-lock/fallback and separate scorer/artifact/missing outcome axes are required, not fully populated.
Latest synthesis leaves task metric/normalization and predeclared missingness to the future task protocol.
C0 already binds controller historical code selection, final refit and hidden MAE after prediction lock; it is not an archive-best policy.

raw_finding.why_it_matters: Keeping all assignments in a ledger is necessary but does not itself define an all-assigned numerical estimand. No lock/no usable artifact, artifact-dependent scorer crash and a lost score for an otherwise valid artifact have different outcome meanings. Complete-case paired differences can select on treatment-dependent success. Unbounded error metrics also have no finite worst-case missing-score bound without an explicit support or sensitivity assumption.
raw_finding.minimum_correction: Bind one task-specific table covering eligible artifact and immutable lock/deadline, incomplete/no lock and any permitted baseline fallback, final refit and scorer timeout/retry, valid poor score, protocol violation, and unobserved score. Freeze score direction, cross-task normalization/weights and aggregation. For unobserved efficacy specify justified bounds/sensitivity assumptions or a non-identifiable result; a separately defined operational utility floor must not be substituted for hidden efficacy. Retain every assignment and all failure/scoring costs.
raw_finding.inexpensive_falsification_check: On paper, apply the analysis to one valid poor score, one no-lock assignment, one locked artifact whose scorer crashes, and one lost scorer receipt. Check that the denominator never silently shrinks, no unknown value becomes zero, and missingness assumptions cannot be changed to reverse the declared conclusion. Also verify that an agent may rationally select a non-best-dev candidate without the evaluator replacing its choice.
raw_finding.uncertainty: No actual missing P0 scientific outcome exists: P0 never started. The future metric, family composition and missingness frequency are unknown; no numeric penalty or attrition rate is proposed.

evidence.detail: P0 House Price family is explicitly development-only even without a score.
Natural versus event-inclusive target population remains unselected.
Family lists and nested repeats are null; correct paired ancestry-unit analysis is required.

Latest decision still defers confirmation task sample to a task-bound protocol.

raw_finding.why_it_matters: An independent sample size cannot be read from the count of task names, contexts or seeds. Related source-data/generator tasks can make the uncertainty too small and allow development decisions to transfer into nominal confirmation. Choosing an event schedule from observed G advantage changes the target population. Shared public exposure may modify a real randomized policy effect; it is not automatically internal confounding, but it limits an unseen-task claim.
raw_finding.minimum_correction: Create the actual future task register with source-data/generator family IDs, shared-library exception, prior human/model exposure where knowable, development membership and the precommitted confirmation sampling procedure. Define the natural/event-inclusive population and any exogenous event release/nonreach policy. Use paired blocks and inference at the actual independent ancestry/assignment unit with nested starts, and state the reachable generalization scope. Preserve House Price exclusion; do not repeat its data preparation.
raw_finding.inexpensive_falsification_check: Blindly relabel a P0-derived re-split and two tasks sharing a data generator in a small metadata-only example. Apply the proposed family rule: renaming must not increase independent n or admit P0 ancestry to confirmation. Check that a programme which never reaches a scheduled event remains in its assigned denominator.
raw_finding.uncertainty: The packet contains no selected future family registry, so actual leakage, between-programme variation and feasible independent sample size were not assessed. No numerical sample-size floor is justified.

raw_finding.domain: development selection, MUE and confirmation precision
raw_finding.phase: Selection procedure and MUE commitment before P1 labelled outcomes; one contrast and analysis before P2

evidence.detail: MUE, power/precision and repeats remain null; development variance must retain estimation uncertainty.
P1 selects candidates/comparator; P2 has one contrast; numeric decision rules and complete mutually exclusive regions remain unset.
MUE/value derivation must be committed before P1 labelled contrast generation or unblinding.
Development selection procedure precedes development outcomes; exact contrast follows P1 and precedes P2 outcomes.
Latest synthesis preserves primary outcome, nested units, MUE timing and no equivalence from nonsignificance.
Valid null/negative and explicitly uncertain closure are allowed; invalid-only results are feasibility, not efficacy.

raw_finding.why_it_matters: A promise to choose the strongest credible comparator is not yet a reproducible selection rule when development data are noisy. If admissibility, ties, cost tradeoffs, MUE or confirmation size are chosen from favourable labelled effects, later interpretation can be tuned to the selected winner. A positive estimate or interval above zero alone need not establish practically useful benefit, and an imprecise null cannot establish equivalence.
raw_finding.minimum_correction: For P1, record a task-value MUE or outcome-independent derivation/owner and exposure timestamp before labelled contrasts; freeze the candidate/comparator selection procedure including feasibility criteria, ties and cost treatment. Use development-only variance/attrition/cost with uncertainty to choose a feasible confirmation precision target and nested-repeat allocation. After P1, freeze exactly one contrast and a complete nonoverlapping efficacy/uncertainty/cost/missingness decision table before P2 reveal. No new P0 efficacy threshold or literature-derived sample number is needed.
raw_finding.inexpensive_falsification_check: Hand-evaluate the proposed selection and decision rules for a tie, a cheaper but slightly worse candidate, a positive-small interval, an interval spanning the MUE, a harmful interval, a wide null and an unidentifiable missingness range. Each must receive exactly one declared disposition; relabelling arms must not alter tie handling or the MUE.
raw_finding.uncertainty: There are no development scores or variance estimates in this packet. Precision and sample size cannot be certified now; the finding concerns missing task-bound rules, not observed optional stopping or biased selection.

raw_finding.minimum_correction: 다음 P1 task-bound 명세에 작은 claim-transition/판정 표를 넣는다. claim text/revision/hash와 task에 필요한 scope 및 source/protocol identity를 묶고, support 승계는 해당 revision·scope에 대한 재판정 결과로 기록한다. contextual/content dependency, 공동필수/대체 support가 해당 task에 존재하면 구별하고, scoped negative·execution failure/UNKNOWN·source correction 각각의 active/qualified/recheck/retracted 결과와 무관 evidence 보존을 예시로 고정한다. 새 graph backend 구현은 필요 없다.

raw_finding.uncertainty: Next action이 이미 기록된 결정을 뜻한다면 실제 충돌은 없다. 현재 문구가 그 의미를 명시하지 않아 발생하는 해석 공백이다. P0에는 별도 exact handoff/기회 보존 계약이 있으며 이를 미정이라고 취급하지 않았다.

findings.title: Assessment-to-successor handoff needs an explicit development/final release discriminator

raw_finding.title: Assessment-to-successor handoff needs an explicit development/final release discriminator

evidence.supports: The shared path connects authoritative terminal receipt plus independent task assessment directly to result and successor decision.
Active policy accepts permitted public observations and must not use hidden scores.
The final scorer has a distinct hidden-data boundary and returns a score/validity receipt.
The detailed scientific contract requires a preselected single artifact and release only after all final locks.
Current P0 requires final assessment after final prediction lock and controller termination, with no score returned for reselection.

raw_finding.current_fact: The detailed study and P0 contracts prohibit hidden-score feedback, while the prototype connection and owner outputs use one generic Result/assessment route. No final-score visibility/release field or consumer rule is specified in that route.
raw_finding.why_it_matters: A future importer could satisfy the drawn assessment-to-successor path while exposing terminal hidden assessment to the still-active research policy. This would change the scientific information set, and accidental differences between C/G would invalidate the intended comparison. Correct prose elsewhere does not define the port message semantics.
raw_finding.smallest_actionable_correction: In the existing handoff row, distinguish DevelopmentObservation from FinalAssessment with programme/phase, assessment kind, artifact lock identity, release condition and allowed consumer. Keep development observations on the online loop; expose hidden final assessment only at the declared post-lock/termination boundary and to a closed-study analysis or an explicitly new programme. Point the row to the existing selection/sealing rules; do not amend frozen P0.
raw_finding.cheap_falsification_check: Later, before adopting the port, walk a small fixture containing a dev score and a hidden-final receipt in the same programme. Before the required locks/termination, only the dev receipt may reach policy input; after closure, final assessment may reach the designated analysis view, with no new same-programme selection. This review did not execute the check.
raw_finding.uncertainty: This is a handoff ambiguity, not evidence of a current leak. The current task-specific bridge does not return a hidden final score in its inspected public/dev result paths. A more specific future typed adapter contract could close the gap.

findings.root_reason: Differentiate development observations and hidden final assessments by release condition, allowed consumer and programme/phase; current P0 already enforces final lock/controller termination, and no live leak was observed.

findings.title: Replay acceptance does not identify the committed decision frontier or distinguish replay from a new model decision

raw_finding.title: Replay acceptance does not identify the committed decision frontier or distinguish replay from a new model decision

evidence.supports: Research state is connected to the session artifact namespace and fresh-session recovery must reconstruct candidate/evidence/latest run/next action.
ResearchEventStore is the single event history and fresh replay is expected to produce the same active revision and next action.
The event-store input/output and active-policy output lists omit a defined committed-decision/frontier record.
Reconciliation lists states and run identity fields but no event commit boundary tied to native recovery/fork.
Snapshotting is best-effort per variable and can return null or skipped values.
Automatic snapshots are debounced, so a completed action can precede its namespace snapshot.
Native fork constructs a new session path and acquires its session lease.
The task bridge writes a durable attempt before prepare/start and later binds identity; this is task apparatus evidence, not a native graph checkpoint contract.

raw_finding.current_fact: The handoff promises deterministic active-state/next-action replay but leaves the durable programme decision frontier, its link to native session/fork IDs, and the distinction between an already committed action and a new LLM choice unspecified.
raw_finding.why_it_matters: Namespace recovery can lag an external action. Re-running a policy is not necessarily deterministic, and a forked session identity must not imply fresh scientific execution authority. Without a shared committed-action record, a future implementation can either change the next action or restore stale pending state while appearing to satisfy normal session recovery. The same ambiguity must not become a G-only recovery capability.
raw_finding.smallest_actionable_correction: Add one concrete checkpoint/decision record to the existing ResearchEventStore contract: programme/arm authority identity, event sequence or parent digest, committed decision and RunIntent identity, policy/projector revision and pending reconciliation frontier. State that replay restores committed decisions; a fresh model proposal is a new event. Declare how resumed/forked sessions reference that same scientific frontier, and which durable artifact survives session lifecycle operations. This is a future task-bound/native handoff requirement, not a request to resume construction.
raw_finding.cheap_falsification_check: Later use a paper or static fixture walkthrough at three cuts: before decision commit, after commit but before launch reply, and after run binding but before kernel snapshot. Resume from a stale snapshot and fork a second session; each must find the same committed decision/frontier, keep ambiguous launch UNKNOWN, and never infer unused budget or permission from the new session ID. No model or live ORX call is needed for the initial check; none was run here.
raw_finding.uncertainty: The packet already specifies conservative UNKNOWN handling and the task bridge implements write-ahead fencing. The gap is their explicit mapping into the proposed native event/replay contract. No claim is made that the inherited session/REPL implementation is defective or that arbitrary fresh LLM choices should be identical.

findings.root_reason: Same recovery/frontier ambiguity as GRAPH-02; retain native snapshot/fork evidence and count as one integrated issue.
